subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Hi Emma

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side around the PII/data handling questions you raised:

TL;DR: We can provide a written confirmation of what Redwood stores for prompts and outputs, where data is stored by region, default retention periods for logs and request traces, and enterprise options for no-logs or customer-managed residency. See the attached one-pager (redwood-pii-data-handling.pdf) for a short table; details below.

What you asked for on the call:
- Do prompts / model outputs get stored on Redwood systems?
- Where (region) is any stored data located?
- Default retention for request logs and any stored prompts/outputs?
- Audit/logging access and who can view raw prompts/outputs?
- Options for no-storage or private deployments (VPC/on-prem)

Initial answers (high level):
- Hosted API (default): request metadata and request/response payloads can be retained for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Default retention is 30 days for prompt/response payloads and 90 days for operational logs and traces.
- Data residency: for Hosted customers we store request payloads in the customer-selected region (e.g., us-east-1) when the account is configured for regional hosting. Enterprise customers can require specific region residency as part of the contract.
- No-logs / Private options: For customers that require zero retention of prompts/outputs, we offer an enterprise "no-logs" agreement or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where customer-managed infrastructure and KMS can eliminate retention on Redwood-hosted storage.
- Access controls & encryption: Data at rest is encrypted with customer/KMS keys for enterprise customers; role-based access controls limit who at Redwood can access raw payloads. All access is logged.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I will send a short written confirmation (this thread) and attach our PII data handling summary (attached).
2) If you want explicit retention exceptions, Rishi will surface the contract language and timeline for a no-logs option.
3) We can schedule a technical follow-up with our infra/security engineer to walk your security team through controls and the SOC 2 report.

If you can confirm the items you need included in the signed statement (retention windows, region, who can access logs), I can convert this into a formal confirmation letter for procurement.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Hi Neha

Thanks for the recap and the one-pager that helps. A few follow-ups from our security/compliance team so we can move to procurement:

1) Can you confirm where the prompt and output payloads are stored physically for our account (we selected US region during onboarding) we need the specific region/availability zone info for our internal inventory.
2) Is the 30-day default retention configurable at the account level? We need the ability to set retention to 0 days for certain workflows that handle PHI.
3) For auditing purposes, who at Redwood has the ability to view raw prompts/outputs, and are those access events included in your audit logs?
4) Does Redwood support automatic prompt redaction (PII masking) at ingestion, or would that be something we implement client-side?

Attached our security questionnaire reference: ACME-SQ-12345.pdf. If you can provide point answers we can insert them into the questionnaire and circulate to procurement.

Best,
Emma Jones
Senior InfoSec Program Manager | Acme Health
emma.jones@acmehealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:30:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Hi Emma

Appreciate the questions answers below (we'll also convert this into the short formal confirmation you can include in ACME-SQ-12345).

1) Physical region: Your account is configured for US (us-east-1). All request payloads for hosted API and logs are stored in the configured region by default. For exact AZ-level details we can provide a hosting region statement for procurement; note that AZs are abstracted in our managed service but all storage remains within the AWS region boundary you selected.

2) Retention configurability: Yes. Default prompts/outputs payload retention is 30 days and operational logs (traces/metrics) default to 90 days. For enterprise customers we offer retention overrides in the contract:
- Option A: 0-day payload retention (no persistent storage of request/response payloads) requires an enterprise no-logs addendum and limited debugging access via a temporary opt-in window.
- Option B: Custom retention window (e.g., 7/14/30/90 days) configurable at account level via support request and contractual agreement.

3) Access controls & audit logging: Only scoped Redwood roles (Support Engineer, Security Ops, and on-call SRE) have the ability to access raw payloads, and that access must be approved through our internal ticketing flow. All accesses are recorded in an immutable audit log (who, when, reason) and retained for 1 year by default (longer retention available under enterprise add-on).

4) Prompt redaction: We do not perform automatic redaction of prompts on behalf of customers by default. Customers can:
- Implement client-side redaction before sending prompts (recommended for PHI).
- Use our enterprise integration for a pre-processing hook (deployed in your VPC) that can apply masking/redaction prior to request delivery to the model.

Other notes:
- Encryption: Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. For enterprise accounts we support customer-managed KMS keys.
- SOC 2 and reports: Our SOC 2 Type II report and controls summary are available to customers under NDA; link to report is in the attached one-pager and the portal link is: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-report

Attached: redwood-pii-data-handling.pdf (includes table of defaults and enterprise options). I also copied Rishi to help with contract language for the no-logs option if you decide to move forward.

Next step: if you confirm you need a 0-day retention addendum for PHI workflows, Rishi will pull together pricing and the legal step. Otherwise, we can schedule the technical deep-dive with your security team next week.

Thanks
Neha
